lines.text: 83% of America's imported avocados come from one country.
lines.say: Eighty-three percent of America's imported avocados come from one country.

lines.text: It's Mexico. And your coffee and generic pills have their own answers.
lines.say: It's Mexico. And your coffee and your generic pills have their own answers.

lines.text: Brazil is the world's biggest coffee producer and exporter.
lines.say: Brazil is the world's biggest coffee producer and exporter.

lines.text: And in 2022, Indian drugmakers supplied 47% of US generic prescriptions.
lines.say: And in twenty twenty-two, Indian drugmakers supplied forty-seven percent of the generic prescriptions filled in the US.

lines.text: India, Brazil and Mexico are three of the world's big emerging markets. Here's how each one makes money, and how it reaches yours.
lines.say: India, Brazil and Mexico are three of the world's big emerging markets. Here's how each one makes its money, and how that reaches yours.

lines.text: Chapter 1: What 'emerging' means.
lines.say: Chapter one: what emerging actually means.

lines.text: The phrase is younger than you'd think. A World Bank economist coined it in 1981.
lines.say: The phrase is younger than you'd think. A World Bank economist coined it in nineteen eighty-one.

lines.text: Antoine van Agtmael at the IFC wanted a better name than 'Third World' for a fund he was pitching.
lines.say: Antoine van Agtmael, at the World Bank's I F C, wanted a better name than Third World for a fund he was pitching.

lines.text: He wanted a name that sounded like growth, not poverty. It stuck.
lines.say: He wanted a name that sounded like growth, not poverty, and it stuck.

lines.text: Today, the best-known stock index of them, from MSCI, covers 24 countries.
lines.say: Today, the best-known stock index of them, from M S C I, covers twenty-four countries.

scene.title: Today, the best-known stock index of them, from

lines.text: There's no single official rule, but emerging markets tend to share a few traits.
lines.say: There's no single official rule, but emerging markets tend to share a few traits.

lines.text: They can grow fast, because they're catching up.
lines.say: They can grow fast, because they're catching up.

lines.text: Their currencies and markets tend to swing more.
lines.say: Their currencies and stock markets tend to swing more.

lines.text: And their financial systems are still being built out.
lines.say: And their financial systems are still being built out.

lines.text: The opposite label is 'developed markets': places like the US, Japan and Germany, with higher incomes and deeper markets.
lines.say: The opposite label is developed markets: places like the US, Japan, and Germany, with higher incomes and deeper financial markets.

scene.caption: The other side of the label

lines.text: Our three are very different, though. Look at output per person in 2026, in the IMF's April estimates.
lines.say: Our three are very different, though. Look at output per person in twenty twenty-six, in the I M F's April estimates.

lines.text: By this measure, Mexico produces about 5.6 times as much per person as India.
lines.say: By this measure, Mexico produces about five point six times as much per person as India.

lines.text: In April, the IMF projected India would grow 6.5% in 2026, versus 1.9% for Brazil and 1.6% for Mexico.
lines.say: In April, the I M F projected India would grow six and a half percent in twenty twenty-six, versus one point nine for Brazil and one point six for Mexico.

lines.text: Poorer and faster, or richer and slower. That's the emerging-market trade-off in one picture.
lines.say: Poorer and faster, or richer and slower. That's the emerging-market trade-off in one picture.

lines.text: Together, these three countries are home to about 1.81 billion people, roughly 22% of everyone on Earth.
lines.say: Together, these three countries are home to about one point eight billion people, roughly twenty-two percent of everyone on Earth.

lines.text: That's why what happens there doesn't stay there.
lines.say: That's why what happens there doesn't stay there.

lines.text: Chapter 2: India, the giant.
lines.say: Chapter two: India, the giant.

lines.text: India has the world's largest population: about 1.46 billion people in 2025, per the UN.
lines.say: India has the world's largest population: about one point four six billion people in twenty twenty-five, according to the U N.

lines.text: India passed China as the most populous country in 2023.
lines.say: India passed China as the most populous country in twenty twenty-three.

lines.text: And they're young. The median age is about 29.
lines.say: And they're young. The median age is about twenty-nine.

lines.text: A young workforce is the engine economists talk about most when they talk about India.
lines.say: A young workforce is the engine economists talk about most when they talk about India.

lines.text: Its economy is big: about $4.15 trillion in 2026, sixth in the world in the IMF's April 2026 ranking.
lines.say: Its economy is big: about four point one five trillion dollars in twenty twenty-six, sixth in the world in the I M F's April twenty twenty-six ranking.

lines.text: But split across nearly 1.48 billion people, that's only about $2,800 each.
lines.say: But split across nearly one point four eight billion people, that's only about twenty-eight hundred dollars each.

lines.text: So how does India earn? A big piece is services: software, call centers and back offices for companies worldwide.
lines.say: So how does India earn? A big piece is services: software, call centers, and back offices for companies around the world.

lines.text: Another is medicine. Indian generics help keep many US prescription prices low.
lines.say: Another is medicine. Indian generics help keep many US prescription prices low.

lines.text: And Indians working abroad send home more money than any other country's workers do.
lines.say: And Indians working abroad send home more money than any other country's workers.

lines.text: India took in $135.4 billion in remittances in the year ending March 2025, the most in the world.
lines.say: India took in a hundred thirty-five point four billion dollars in remittances in the year that ended March twenty twenty-five, the most in the world.

lines.text: Spread across the whole country, that's about $93 per person a year.
lines.say: Spread across the whole country, that's about ninety-three dollars per person a year.

lines.text: But it's concentrated. For families with a worker abroad, it can be the biggest paycheck in the house.
lines.say: But it's concentrated. For families with a worker abroad, it can be the biggest paycheck in the house.

lines.text: Now the currency. In 2021, a dollar bought about 73.94 rupees on average.
lines.say: Now, the currency. In twenty twenty-one, a dollar bought about seventy-four rupees on average.

scene.title: Rupees per US dollar (Fed, annual avg)

lines.text: By 2025, it bought 87.15. The rupee got weaker against the dollar every year.
lines.say: By twenty twenty-five, it bought about eighty-seven. The rupee got weaker against the dollar every single year.

scene.title: Rupees per US dollar (Fed, annual avg)

lines.text: So $100 bought 7,394 rupees in 2021, and 8,715 in 2025. That's 1,321 more.
lines.say: So a hundred dollars bought about seventy-four hundred rupees in twenty twenty-one, and about eighty-seven hundred in twenty twenty-five. That's thirteen hundred more.

lines.text: A weaker rupee helps India's exporters sell abroad, and makes imports like oil cost more at home.
lines.say: A weaker rupee helps India's exporters sell abroad, and makes imports like oil cost more at home.

lines.text: Here's why. A $1,000 software contract paid in dollars brought in 73,940 rupees in 2021, and 87,150 in 2025.
lines.say: Here's why. A thousand-dollar software contract paid in dollars brought in about seventy-four thousand rupees in twenty twenty-one, and about eighty-seven thousand in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Same work, about 18% more rupees, without raising the price in dollars.
lines.say: Same work, about eighteen percent more rupees, without raising the price in dollars.

lines.text: India's central bank sets a key rate, the repo rate. As of September 2026, it was 5.25%.
lines.say: India's central bank sets a key rate called the repo rate. As of September twenty twenty-six, it was five and a quarter percent.

lines.text: It's the same tool the Fed uses here: lower rates make loans cheaper, higher rates cool prices down.
lines.say: It's the same tool the Fed uses here. Lower rates make loans cheaper, and higher rates help cool prices down.

lines.text: Chapter 3: Brazil, the farm.
lines.say: Chapter three: Brazil, the farm.

lines.text: Brazil has about 212.8 million people, and the IMF put its economy at about $2.64 trillion in 2026, as of April.
lines.say: Brazil has about two hundred thirteen million people, and the I M F put its economy at about two point six four trillion dollars in twenty twenty-six, as of April.

lines.text: The IMF puts that at about $12,300 per person, more than four times India's.
lines.say: The I M F puts that at about twelve thousand three hundred dollars per person, more than four times India's.

lines.text: Brazil earns a lot from what grows and what's dug up: soybeans, coffee, beef, iron ore and oil.
lines.say: Brazil earns a lot from what grows and what gets dug up: soybeans, coffee, beef, iron ore, and oil.

lines.text: Its biggest customer isn't the US. It's China.
lines.say: Its biggest customer isn't the US. It's China.

lines.text: From January to October 2025, about 80% of Brazil's soybean exports went to China.
lines.say: From January to October twenty twenty-five, about eighty percent of Brazil's soybean exports went to China.

scene.label: Brazil soybean exports to China, Jan-Oct 2025

lines.text: That's a strength and a risk. When one buyer takes most of the crop, its choices move your prices.
lines.say: That's a strength and a risk. When one buyer takes most of the crop, that buyer's choices move your prices.

lines.text: Commodity countries ride booms and busts. When crop and metal prices rise, money pours in. When they fall, it dries up.
lines.say: Commodity countries ride booms and busts. When crop and metal prices rise, money pours in. When they fall, it dries up.

lines.text: Brazil's other famous number is its interest rate. The central bank's Selic rate is very high.
lines.say: Brazil's other famous number is its interest rate. The central bank's Selic rate is very high.

lines.text: On September 16, 2026, it cut the Selic to 13.75%, its fifth straight quarter-point cut, down from 15%.
lines.say: On September sixteenth, twenty twenty-six, it cut the Selic to thirteen point seven five percent, its fifth straight quarter-point cut, down from fifteen.

lines.text: High rates are how Brazil fights inflation. They also make borrowing painful for Brazilian families and businesses.
lines.say: High rates are how Brazil fights inflation. They also make borrowing painful for Brazilian families and businesses.

lines.text: High rates also attract foreign savers chasing yield. Their risk: if Brazil's currency falls, the dollar value of that interest can shrink.
lines.say: High rates also attract foreign savers chasing yield. Their risk is that if Brazil's currency falls, the dollar value of that interest can shrink.

lines.text: That's the emerging-market bargain in a nutshell: higher potential reward, with more ways for things to go wrong.
lines.say: That's the emerging-market bargain in a nutshell: higher potential reward, with more ways for things to go wrong.

lines.text: For comparison, India's key rate was 5.25% and Mexico's was 6.5% in September 2026.
lines.say: For comparison, India's key rate was five and a quarter percent and Mexico's was six and a half in September twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: And for you: Brazil's harvests are a big reason coffee costs what it does.
lines.say: And for you, Brazil's harvests are a big reason coffee costs what it does.

lines.text: A frost or drought in Brazil's coffee belt can ripple all the way to your morning cup.
lines.say: A frost or a drought in Brazil's coffee belt can ripple all the way to your morning cup.

lines.text: Chapter 4: Mexico, the neighbor.
lines.say: Chapter four: Mexico, the neighbor.

lines.text: Mexico has about 132 million people and the highest output per person of our three: $15,779 in 2026.
lines.say: Mexico has about a hundred thirty-two million people, and the highest output per person of our three: about fifteen thousand eight hundred dollars in twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: Its big advantage is geography. It shares a border of nearly 2,000 miles with the world's biggest consumer market.
lines.say: Its big advantage is geography. It shares a border of nearly two thousand miles with the world's biggest consumer market.

scene.caption: Next door to the biggest market

lines.text: In 2025, Mexico was America's top trading partner in goods: $872.8 billion both ways.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, Mexico was America's top trading partner in goods, with eight hundred seventy-three billion dollars flowing both ways.

lines.text: Cars, auto parts, electronics and food cross that border every day, often more than once.
lines.say: Cars, auto parts, electronics, and food cross that border every day, often more than once.

lines.text: Companies also talk about 'nearshoring': moving factories closer to US customers, often from Asia to Mexico.
lines.say: Companies also talk about nearshoring, which means moving factories closer to US customers, often from Asia to Mexico.

lines.text: Shorter trips mean less shipping time, and fewer things that can go wrong on the way.
lines.say: Shorter trips mean less shipping time, and fewer things that can go wrong along the way.

lines.text: A part can be made in Michigan, finished in Mexico, then come back in a car.
lines.say: A part can be made in Michigan, finished in Mexico, then come back inside a finished car.

lines.text: The trade gap has grown. In 1993, the US ran a $1.7 billion goods surplus with Mexico. In 2025, it ran a $171.5 billion deficit.
lines.say: The trade gap has grown. In nineteen ninety-three, the US ran a one point seven billion dollar goods surplus with Mexico. In twenty twenty-five, it ran a hundred seventy-one point five billion dollar deficit.

lines.text: A deficit means Americans bought more from Mexico than they sold there. It doesn't mean money vanished.
lines.say: A deficit means Americans bought more from Mexico than they sold there. It doesn't mean money vanished.

lines.text: Food is part of it. The US imported 2.7 billion pounds of fresh avocados in 2025, and 83% came from Mexico.
lines.say: Food is part of it. The US imported two point seven billion pounds of fresh avocados in twenty twenty-five, and eighty-three percent came from Mexico.

lines.text: That's about 2.24 billion pounds from Mexico alone.
lines.say: That's about two and a quarter billion pounds from Mexico alone.

lines.text: Money also flows the other way. Mexicans abroad, mostly in the US, sent home $61.8 billion in 2025.
lines.say: Money also flows the other way. Mexicans abroad, mostly in the US, sent home sixty-one point eight billion dollars in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: That was down 4.6%, the biggest drop since 2009. Families in Mexico felt it in 2025.
lines.say: That was down four point six percent, the biggest drop since two thousand nine, and families in Mexico felt it in twenty twenty-five.

lines.text: Per person, that's about $468 a year in Mexico, versus about $93 in India.
lines.say: Per person, that's about four hundred sixty-eight dollars a year in Mexico, versus about ninety-three in India.

lines.text: Mexico's central bank held its rate at 6.5% on September 24, 2026, for a third straight meeting.
lines.say: Mexico's central bank held its rate at six and a half percent on September twenty-fourth, twenty twenty-six, for a third straight meeting.

lines.text: The catch with being next door: when US demand or trade rules change, Mexico feels it first.
lines.say: The catch with being next door is that when US demand or trade rules change, Mexico feels it first.

lines.text: Tariffs between the US and all three of these countries have swung a lot since 2025, and that shows up in prices.
lines.say: Tariffs between the US and all three of these countries have swung a lot since twenty twenty-five, and that shows up in prices.

lines.text: Chapter 5: How it reaches your wallet.
lines.say: Chapter five: how it reaches your wallet.

lines.text: Route one is the grocery store and the pharmacy.
lines.say: Route one is the grocery store and the pharmacy.

lines.text: A bad Brazilian coffee harvest, a Mexican avocado slowdown or an Indian drug-plant problem can all show up in what you pay.
lines.say: A bad Brazilian coffee harvest, a Mexican avocado slowdown, or a problem at an Indian drug plant can all show up in what you pay.

lines.text: Route two is the dollar. When the dollar is strong, imports from these countries tend to get cheaper for you.
lines.say: Route two is the dollar. When the dollar is strong, imports from these countries tend to get cheaper for you.

lines.text: Many target-date and international funds hold emerging-market stocks, often by tracking an index like MSCI's.
lines.say: Many target-date and international funds hold emerging-market stocks, often by tracking an index like M S C I's.

lines.text: That means swings in Mumbai, São Paulo or Mexico City can show up on your statement, in either direction.
lines.say: That means swings in Mumbai, São Paulo, or Mexico City can show up on your statement, in either direction.

lines.text: That's not a reason to buy or avoid anything. It's a reason to know what you already own.
lines.say: That's not a reason to buy or avoid anything. It's a reason to know what you already own.

lines.text: One more thing: a fast-growing economy doesn't guarantee fast-growing stocks. Prices can already reflect the growth.
lines.say: One more thing: a fast-growing economy doesn't guarantee fast-growing stocks, because prices can already reflect the growth.

lines.text: Chapter 6: Recap.
lines.say: Chapter six: the recap.

lines.text: India: huge, young and the fastest-growing of the three, with about $2,813 of output per person.
lines.say: India is huge, young, and the fastest-growing of the three, with about twenty-eight hundred dollars of output per person.

lines.text: Brazil: a farm and a mine for the world, selling most of its soybeans to China, with a 13.75% interest rate as of September.
lines.say: Brazil is a farm and a mine for the world, selling most of its soybeans to China, with a thirteen point seven five percent interest rate as of September.

lines.text: Mexico: the richest per person of the three, and America's top goods trading partner.
lines.say: Mexico is the richest per person of the three, and America's top goods trading partner.

lines.text: 'Emerging' sounds like one club. It's really three very different economies, all tied to your groceries, your prices and maybe your 401(k).
lines.say: Emerging sounds like one club. It's really three very different economies, all tied to your groceries, your prices, and maybe your four oh one K.

post.yt_desc:
India, Brazil and Mexico are three of the world's biggest emerging markets, and they work in very different ways. This video explains what 'emerging markets' means, how India earns from services, generic drugs and the world's largest remittances; how Brazil earns from soybeans, coffee and commodities with a 13.75% interest rate as of September 2026; and how Mexico became America's top goods trading partner. It ends with three ways these economies reach an American's wallet.
